title: Normalized finite-discrete encoding commutes with inverse image
statement: For finite discrete commutative A, every scheme morphism f:U→T and normalized encodings E_T,E_U, the fixed-module encoding of f* M is naturally isomorphic to the fixed-module inverse image of the encoding of M. Definitions and encodings are those of [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding].

source.place: Second paragraph: the finite-stalk constructibility convention used for all quotient coefficients.

proof.text: Read the section action using normalization: a acts by the internal action of the canonical constant section.
Naturality of canonical constant sections makes the identity of section groups linear between the two direct images; these identities give a natural isomorphism.
Conjugate this right-adjoint isomorphism by the encoding equivalences and the specified inverse-image adjunctions. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives the comparison.

theorem encoding_pullback_fixed [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A]
    {T U : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ T) (eT : Encoding A T) (eU : Encoding A U)
    (M : Internal A T) :
    Nonempty ((eU.ordinary.functor ⋙ eU.fixed.functor).obj
        ((CondensedRing.upperStar (coefficient A) f).obj M) ≅
      (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)) f).obj
        ((eT.ordinary.functor ⋙ eT.fixed.functor).obj M))
